title: Loopio vs Responsive (2026): Features, Reviews, Limitations, and Alternatives
summary: Loopio vs Responsive compared on AI, pricing, support, and G2 ratings, plus who each fits and the per-RFP alternative both leave room for. See the verdict.
body_markdown:
If you are shortlisting[RFP software](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/best-rfp-software) , Loopio and Responsive are almost always the two tools you end up comparing. Both are established, well-reviewed, and built on the same traditional model: a content library your team maintains, with AI added on top.


So when you compare Loopio and Responsive, two questions matter: which of the two fits your team, and whether a library-based platform fits your team at all. This guide covers both, so you can decide with the full picture.


***Last reviewed: September 2026. This comparison is based on vendor-published materials, verified G2 and Capterra reviews, and independent third-party analyses. Pricing and feature details change over time, so confirm current specifics directly with each vendor before purchasing.***


## **TL;DR**


- Choose Loopio for ease of use, the best-rated support in the category, and fast rollout for a focused team.
- Choose Responsive for enterprise scale, 23+ languages, intake, and program-wide reporting, if you can absorb a steeper learning curve and a per-user bill.
- On G2, Loopio holds 4.6/5 (813 reviews) and Responsive 4.5/5 (1,312 reviews).
- Both are legacy content-library tools with AI added on top, so your team maintains the library and runs each step. If that upkeep or[per-seat pricing](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/rfp-software-pricing) is your blocker, an AI-native platform like Inventive AI, where agents draft and your team approves, is worth a look.

## **What is Loopio? A library-first RFP response platform**


Loopio is an RFP and response management platform founded in Toronto in 2014. Teams use it to respond to[RFPs](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/what-is-rfp) , security questionnaires, and due diligence requests from a central content library, with structured workflows and strong collaboration. Loopio was built around that library first, and its AI, branded Magic, was added on top later. It suggests matches from your approved content rather than drafting each response on its own, so the library stays the engine and the AI is a layer over it.


## **What is Responsive (formerly RFPIO)? A response management platform**


Responsive, formerly RFPIO, is an enterprise response management platform for RFPs, security questionnaires,[government bids](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/best-government-proposal-software) , and DDQs. It markets itself as AI-first, but its AI Assistant and agents were added on top of the Q&A-library architecture the platform was originally built on. That foundation gives it enterprise depth and broad integrations, and it also means the AI sits over a library your team still curates and maintains.

## **Responsive vs Loopio: features, limitations, and reviews**


Here is the full Responsive vs Loopio comparison, tool by tool: key features, limitations, pricing, and what G2 and Capterra reviewers say about each.


### **Loopio**


Loopio Product Image


### ‍ **Loopio key features**


- Centralized content library with stacks, categories, and tags
- Magic AI for one-click response suggestions from approved content
- Milestone tracking and SME assignment for project management
- Content analytics for library health and completion tracking
- Portal based response capability, added recently
- Chrome extension for filling out questionnaires inside client portals


#### **Loopio limitations**


- AI is limited to suggesting matches from a static library. It doesn't generate context-aware drafts, so responses often still need heavy rewriting.
- No conflict detection. Contradictory or outdated answers across the library go unnoticed unless a human catches them.
- No competitive intelligence agents. Nothing in the platform helps research competitors or build[win themes](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/creating-effective-rfp-win-themes) .
- No deal-specific personalization. Every buyer gets pulled from the same global library, regardless of the RFP or opportunity.
- No inline source citations, so tracing an AI suggestion back to its origin means a manual lookup.
- User-based pricing penalizes teams that need to loop in many occasional SMEs.
- Manual library upkeep is required and becomes harder to manage without a dedicated owner, a common reason teams start exploring[Loopio alternatives](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/loopio-alternatives)


#### **Loopio pricing**


- [Loopio pricing](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/loopio-pricing-features-reviews) follows a seat-based tier model (Foundations, Enhanced, and Enterprise) and is not published; onboarding packages, translations, and industry integrations are sold as add-ons
- According to[Vendr’s transaction data](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/loopio) , typical annual contracts range from $15,000 to $150,000+
- Mid-market deployments (10–25 users) typically fall in the $30,000–$60,000 annual range


#### **Loopio ratings and reviews**


- **G2:** 4.6/5
- **Capterra:** 4.6/5
- **TrustRadius:** 8/10

## **Loopio vs Responsive: AI-native Feature Comparison**


Here is a deeper look at the AI-native capabilities proposal and[security teams](https://www.inventive.ai/solution/it-and-security-teams) screen for, from autonomous agents to content governance, and how much of each Loopio and Responsive actually deliver.


### **AI agents for end-to-end automation**


- **Loopio:** No end-to-end agent. Loopio runs a human-in-the-loop model: its Magic AI surfaces and suggests matching answers from your approved library, and a person assembles, edits, and finalizes the response. It speeds up retrieval, but the drafting workflow is still driven by your team at each step.
- **Responsive:** Partial. Its AI Assistant and agents generate full first drafts across RFPs,[DDQs](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/best-ddq-software) , and[security questionnaires](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/best-security-questionnaire-automation-software) , mapping incoming questions to content and prepopulating answers. The automation is real, but it sits on top of the legacy Q&A library rather than orchestrating intake, drafting, validation, and flagging as one autonomous flow.


### **Go/no-go agent**


- **Loopio:** Available as a paid add-on. It scores opportunity fit and lets you weigh named competitors to support the[qualification decision](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/go-no-go-decision-projects) , so confirm it is included before you assume you have it.
- **Responsive:** Included. Bid/no-bid fit scoring evaluates an incoming opportunity against your criteria so teams can[decide whether to pursue or pass](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/when-to-decline-rfp) before investing hours in a response.


### **Automatic response analyzer**


- **Loopio:** No full-response analyzer. Quality control is manual, answer by answer, through SME review, so catching gaps or inconsistencies across a long response depends on the reviewer.
- **Responsive:** Partial, through TRACE Score. It validates individual responses for quality and confidence signals, which helps reviewers prioritize. It checks answers one at a time, so cross-section contradictions and tone consistency across the whole document still need a human pass.


### **Automatic content governance**


- **Loopio:** Partial. Response Intelligence detects duplicates, cleans up content, and enriches metadata to keep the library tidy. Keeping answers accurate and current still runs on manual SME review cycles, and it does not automatically flag when two answers conflict.
- **Responsive:** Partial. Metadata tagging and TRACE-driven validation support governance at scale, and content can be linked across versions. It still relies on periodic human review to catch drift, and does not automatically detect contradictory answers across the library.


### **Integrations**


- **Loopio:** Connects to Salesforce and[HubSpot](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations/hubspot-for-rfp-automation) for CRM workflows,[Slack](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations/slack-rfp-automation) and[Teams for collaboration](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations/microsoft-teams-rfp-automation) , and 80+ content sources like SharePoint and Google Drive, plus a Chrome extension for answering questionnaires inside client portals. API support covers standard use cases.
- **Responsive:** A broader enterprise layer, with around 30 native integrations and 75+ open APIs. It aligns more deeply with enterprise CRM,[sales enablement](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/best-ai-tools-sales-enablement) , and productivity stacks, and pushes content into tools like Salesforce and Microsoft for real-time access during the sales cycle.


### **Analytics**


- **Loopio:** Reporting on library health, proposal performance, and response completion times, aimed at keeping a focused team's content current and projects on track.
- **Responsive:** Advanced reporting and dashboards built for scale, tracking performance across large teams and many concurrent projects, which suits program-level oversight.


### **User interface**


- **Loopio:** Users consistently call the interface clean and intuitive, and say it is easy to train new people on, which is one of the top reasons teams pick it. Some note a learning curve on advanced features, and occasional admin-permission friction when trying to reach completed questions.
- **Responsive:** . Many users find it intuitive, while others describe the interface as cluttered and not intuitive, call it clunky or dated, and say common tasks take more clicks than they should. Onboarding, on the other hand, is well regarded, with users pointing to structured training and a smooth setup.


Two capabilities neither platform fully delivers- agent-driven end-to-end automation and automatic content governance with conflict detection- are the gaps buyers raise most in evaluations. That is why teams comparing Loopio and Responsive increasingly put an AI-native platform on the shortlist too.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is Loopio or Responsive better?


It depends on your team. Loopio is better for focused teams that want ease of use, fast onboarding, and top-rated support. Responsive is better for large enterprises that need deep integrations, many languages, and program-wide reporting. On G2, Loopio holds 4.6/5 and Responsive 4.5/5.


### Is Responsive the same as RFPIO?


Yes. Responsive is the current name for the platform formerly known as RFPIO. The rebrand did not change its core RFP and response management capabilities.


### Which is easier to use, Loopio or Responsive?


Loopio. Reviewers consistently describe its interface as clean and easy to train people on. Responsive is more powerful but denser, and some users find it cluttered with a steeper learning curve.


### Which has better AI, Loopio or Responsive?


Responsive has the more capable AI for drafting: it generates full first responses, while Loopio's AI suggests matches from your approved library rather than drafting from scratch. Output from both still needs a human review pass, and reviewers report occasional hallucination with Responsive.


### How much do Loopio and Responsive cost?


Both are quote-based with no public list pricing. Loopio is tier-based by users and features; third-party data puts typical contracts between $15,000 and $150,000+ a year. Responsive starts around $5,000 a year for five users on its Lite plan, with mid and enterprise tiers custom-quoted. Both charge by user, so cost rises as you add people.


### Which is better for enterprise versus a smaller team?


Responsive is built for large, multi-department enterprises with high volume and complex workflows. Loopio fits focused and mid-sized teams that value speed and simplicity. For long-form narrative bids and government proposals, Responsive is the more common choice; for structured RFPs and security questionnaires, Loopio is a strong fit.


### How do I migrate from Loopio or Responsive to another tool?


Your response library is exportable from both platforms, so you keep your approved content. AI-native tools can import and de-duplicate that content during onboarding, which means you start from your existing answers rather than a blank slate. Ask any new vendor to run one of your recent RFPs during the evaluation so you see real output on your content.


### Is there an AI-native alternative to Loopio and Responsive?


Yes. A newer category of AI-native platforms, including Inventive AI, takes a different approach: autonomous agents draft from your connected knowledge and keep content current automatically, which reduces the manual library maintenance that both Loopio and Responsive require.
